_description: Recall Lab mechanism-class taxonomy. Each awarded eval finding is tagged with a mechanism_class in adjudication.json; the scoreboard reports per-class recall so we can see which expert-bug FAMILIES the system systematically misses (independent of project). 'prompt_section' points at the specialist agent section that teaches the class (the proven cold-recall lever). status: caught=system reliably finds it; reincorporated=prompt section authored after a miss; design=opinion/non-mechanical (not prompt-addressable); coverage=miss was a read-coverage gap not a reasoning gap; SEEDED=authored a-priori for a NEW language (Rust/Solana), NOT yet eval-validated (to be confirmed/upgraded by the recall lab). 'language' field (default solidity) keeps cross-language classes out of the Solidity scoreboard until earned.
_solana_seed_note: The solana-* classes below are SEEDED (language:rust, status:seeded) from public Solana audit knowledge; they are scaffolding for the Rust recall-lab bootstrap (P4) and are validated/upgraded to 'reincorporated' only when a scored Solana contest confirms them. They never count toward Solidity recall.
_move_seed_note: The move-* classes below are SEEDED (language:move, status:seeded) from Sui/Move audit knowledge (Cetus $220M CLMM class + general Sui object/capability review); scaffolding for the Move recall-lab bootstrap. They are language-tagged so they NEVER count toward Solidity or Rust recall scoring.

move-address-param-not-signer-auth.description: an owner/admin/identity check compares against an address VALUE supplied by the caller as a function parameter (e.g. assert!(caller == @owner) where caller: address is an arg) instead of deriving authority from possession — signer::address_of(&signer) (Aptos) / tx_context::sender (Sui) / a Cap — so any account passes the privileged address and the assert holds for an attacker

evm-insecure-onchain-randomness.description: an EVM security/economic outcome (lottery/raffle winner, reward/airdrop amount, NFT trait/rarity, tier, ordering) is seeded from on-chain-observable or proposer-influenceable state - block.timestamp, block.number, blockhash (0 outside 256 blocks), block.prevrandao/difficulty (known to the proposer pre-build, biasable by slot-skipping), msg.sender, or a public counter - so it is predictable/manipulable (incl. revert-to-re-roll via a wrapper contract); correct = Chainlink VRF or commit-reveal. Generalized from the Move pizza-drop M-01 finding; EVM-eval-validated on eggstravaganza H-01 (blind fleet, economic_attack cited §12).

solana-insecure-onchain-randomness.description: a Solana security/economic outcome (lottery/raffle winner, reward/airdrop amount, NFT trait/rarity, tier, ordering) is seeded from on-chain-observable or leader-influenceable state - Clock unix_timestamp/slot/epoch, SlotHashes/recent blockhash, a Pubkey, or a public counter - so it is predictable/manipulable (incl. abort-to-re-roll via a wrapper/CPI); correct = a VRF/oracle (Switchboard VRF) or commit-reveal. SEEDED, generalized from the Move pizza-drop M-01 finding; not yet Solana-eval-validated.

move-insecure-onchain-randomness.description: a security/economic outcome (reward amount, winner, tier, NFT trait, ordering) is seeded from on-chain-observable or proposer-influenceable state — timestamp::now_*(), block height/epoch, an address, or a counter (often with % N) — so it is predictable/manipulable; ALSO covers the Aptos test-and-abort (selective-abort) biasing where a publicly-wrappable #[randomness] entry lets an attacker re-roll for free by aborting unfavorable draws. Correct = aptos_framework::randomness from a non-wrappable caller, or commit-reveal.

move-onchain-data-not-private.description: a value meant to be confidential (secret/password/seed/off-chain key/preimage-before-reveal) is stored in plaintext in an on-chain resource/object; all on-chain state is world-readable by any full node/RPC/indexer regardless of the Move visibility of the gating functions, so the data leaks the moment it is written — access-control on a #[view]/getter is irrelevant to raw storage reads (must be hashed/committed/encrypted)

solana-missing-signer-check.description: an instruction that performs a privileged action (incl. INIT of config/oracle/pool) does not gate the caller (no Signer assertion / no authority|admin check) → anyone can invoke or initialize as if authorized

solana-missing-owner-check.description: a passed account is deserialized/trusted without verifying account.owner == expected program id (or Anchor Account<T> type) → attacker substitutes a look-alike account they control

solana-account-substitution-confusion.description: two accounts of compatible layout (or missing discriminator/type check) let an attacker pass account A where B is expected (type confusion / arbitrary-account substitution) ALSO (LZ executor H-3.2): a PRIVILEGED Signer/account passed by-ref into an attacker-controlled CPI (here remaining_accounts forwarded to invoke()) can be REASSIGNED/written by the callee — its owner/data must be RE-VALIDATED after the CPI (fix added require!(executor.owner==system_program && data_is_empty())).

solana-missing-anchor-constraint.description: an Anchor account is missing a needed #[account(...)] constraint (has_one / seeds / address / mut / close / token::authority / a cross-field equality) that a sibling account or protocol invariant requires → unauthorized mutation/relation. e.g. WOOFi quote-pool: woopool_quote.token_mint==quote checked but NOT woopool_quote.token_mint==woopool_quote.quote_token_mint, so a non-quote pool's reserve is charged the fee ALSO: cross-chain handlers (lz_receive) where the recipient/token ACCOUNTS passed by the caller are not bound to the authenticated MESSAGE fields (user==receiver, deposit_token==token_hash) — the endpoint clear() authenticates the message, NOT the Solana accounts; an off-chain *_types account-list hint does NOT enforce on-chain (Orderly H-1 deposit_token!=allowed_token.mint_account; H-2 user!=withdraw receiver).

solana-reinit-missing-init-guard.description: an account can be re-initialized (no init_if_needed guard / no already-initialized check / init not enforced) → state reset or takeover (Solana analog of init-once-guard-missing)

solana-close-account-revival.description: an account closed without zeroing data / not using Anchor close (lamports drained but data intact, or no realloc-zero) → revived within same tx / reused (close-then-reinit attack) ALSO (LZ uln H-3.1 'arbitrary ULN PDAs can be closed'): a `close = receiver` instruction gated ONLY by a Signer whose key is itself part of the PDA seeds (any keypair can be that 'dvn'), with an UNCHECKED `receiver: AccountInfo` for the reclaimed rent. Result: state PDAs (DVN confirmations) can be closed by an unauthorized party / rent redirected. RULE: a close must validate WHO may close (real authority, not a self-derived-seed signer) AND, if rent matters, constrain the receiver.

solana-pda-seed-collision.description: PDA seeds are not canonical/bump-checked or are user-controllable so two logical entities map to the same PDA (or a non-canonical bump is accepted) → state collision / spoofed authority

solana-cpi-arbitrary-program.description: a CPI invokes a program id taken from an account/arg without verifying it equals the expected program (e.g. token program id unchecked) → attacker routes the CPI to a malicious program

solana-remaining-accounts-trust.description: ctx.remaining_accounts entries are used without validating owner/key/signer → attacker injects arbitrary accounts the handler trusts ALSO (LZ uln M-3.3): the remaining_accounts SLICE LENGTH was derived from the WRONG config field (optional_dvn_threshold instead of optional_dvns.len()), so a downstream loop indexing accounts[offset+i] over ALL optional DVNs runs past the slice -> out-of-bounds PANIC / DoS. Cross-check that the count used to slice remaining_accounts matches the count the consumer iterates.

solana-arithmetic-unchecked.description: lamport/token arithmetic uses unchecked +/-/* (not checked_add/checked_sub) in release (overflow-checks off) → silent wrap draining funds (Rust analog of arithmetic overflow; the compiler does NOT save you in release) DIVISION sub-checks (Drift): (1) `.div(x)` instead of `checked_div(x)` PANICS on x==0 — any divisor that can reach 0 (e.g. base_asset_amount, a reserve) is a DoS; require checked_div + explicit zero guard. (2) SIGNED integer division rounds TOWARD ZERO (positive floored, negative ceiled), so a precision-reducing div of a signed value (funding/PnL) is ASYMMETRIC → systematic accounting bias favoring one side; pick an explicit rounding direction that doesn't leak value to users.

solana-pda-signer-seeds-missing-bump.description: a PDA's seeds() used for invoke_signed/CpiContext::new_with_signer omits the canonical bump (or a required seed), so the derived signer != the PDA → the CPI signature is invalid and the privileged CPI (vault payout) permanently fails / funds stuck

solana-init-authority-mismatch-vs-use.description: an account field (authority/owner) is set at INIT to the creator (msg.sender/admin), but a LATER instruction's constraint requires that field to equal a DIFFERENT authority (e.g. manager.authority) → accounts created by a non-matching creator are permanently unusable in the later instruction (claim/withdraw bricked)

solana-duplicate-mutable-account-seriali.description: an instruction takes >=2 mutable accounts of the same type that CAN be the same account (aliased); Anchor serializes in-memory copies at the end so only one write survives → lost state update (e.g. fee credited to woopool_quote is overwritten when woopool_to==woopool_quote). Forbid aliasing (key!=key) or operate on one reloaded instance

signed-validity-window.description: auth/time metadata appended to a signature but not covered by the signed hash (relayer-malleable)

inclusive-boundary-snapshot.description: inclusive timestamp/epoch boundary in reward/snapshot lookups lets a boundary checkpoint retroactively qualify for the prior period

cross-function-conservation.description: one-sided backing/solvency accounting — an asset side (e.g. borrow liabilities) omitted from a backing/surplus aggregation across functions

lock-unlock-monotonicity.description: lock/unlock-time set/overwrite without a monotonicity guard (extend grief or early-unlock)

missing-sibling-check.description: an action has a paired/sibling guard (approve vs disapprove, add vs remove) but one side omits the check, enabling contradictory state

remainder-carryover.description: per-unit remainder/dust carryover reused across calls or wrongly reset to 0, enabling inflation or unit bypass

accrual-parity.description: a state-changing setter skips the harvest/accrual that sibling mutators perform, desyncing rewards

fee-accounting-shared-position.description: fees accrued on a shared LP/AMM position mis-attributed so most users cannot claim their share

self-whitelist-bypass.description: an access gate (whitelist/allowlist) can be satisfied by the caller themselves (e.g. via receive()/self-registration)

single-sided-liquidity-grief.description: a one-time lifecycle action (launch/finalize) can be permanently griefed by single-sided/asymmetric input

lp-burn-slippage.description: an LP burn/claim returns amounts without slippage bounds, exposing the caller to manipulation

transferable-position-cap-bypass.description: a per-user cap invariant is bypassed by transferring the position NFT/token between accounts

hand-rolled-index.description: hand-rolled array/index bookkeeping (overlap checks, swap-pop, per-selector lists) mishandles boundaries -> legitimate inputs revert

unbounded-array-griefing.description: an unbounded growable set iterated in a critical/single-shot path -> gas griefing/DoS by inflating the set

self-bricking-setter.description: a timelocked/guarded parameter setter whose own precondition makes the change un-executable (bricks its own update)

post-op-invariant-comparison.description: wrong comparison/operands in a post-operation health/invariant check (e.g. liquidation solvency)

external-call-return-check.description: assumes an external call/stake reverts on failure; missing return-value check -> silent failure

burnable-token-design.description: design-opinion finding (e.g. token should be burnable) — not a mechanical bug; not prompt-addressable

cross-service-reentrancy.description: a per-entity reentrancy guard (zero the current id's field before transfer) doesn't stop re-entry via a SIBLING id/service/position against a shared pool

signature-missing-deadline.description: signed (EIP-712) operation omits a deadline from the signed struct → signature valid forever / replayable

signature-missing-parameter.description: an outcome-affecting parameter (e.g. max bond, amount, recipient) is consumed by the call but not bound into the signed struct → submitter controls it

effectivebond-no-downward-correction.description: a monotonic accumulator is credited upward when recomputed>stored but has no symmetric downward branch → over-credits permanently

checkpoint-timing-manipulation.description: permissionless checkpoint/settlement of rate*elapsed rewards lets the caller time it (around droughts/refills or eligibility snapshots) to capture undeserved rewards

init-once-guard-missing.description: a standalone/cloned helper deployed uninitialized exposes init()/initialize() with no init-once guard and no caller restriction → attacker seizes admin and drains

default-sentinel-reward-routing-jit.description: a fee/commission/reward share routed by a default/sentinel code (==0) is claimable by anyone → JIT-captured right before distribution with no prior contribution

critical-path-math-revert-dos.description: valuation/collateral/health math on a critical path (mint/liquidate/withdraw) reverts on legitimate edge inputs (div-by-zero at zero distance, out-of-domain getSqrtRatioAtTick, unchecked threshold-balance subtraction underflow for insolvent accounts) → position unmanageable/unliquidatable

unreachable-guard-branch-ordering.description: a safety/divergence/solvency guard is present in source but rendered unreachable (dead code) by condition placement / branch ordering / early-return → protection never fires (partial->strong: complete the reachability trace instead of hedging on guard effectiveness)

bad-debt-socialization-par-exit.description: a withdraw/redeem prices shares at a stale par rate that excludes unrealized bad debt → first-mover exits whole and socializes the shortfall onto remaining LPs (bank-run race)

position-nft-callback-liquidation-dos.description: safeTransferFrom of a position-NFT to the owner on a must-complete path (liquidation cleanup) hands control to onERC721Received which REVERTS to make the owner un-liquidatable (DoS variant of the re-enter-to-mutate hook bug)

oracle-decimal-scaling-overflow.description: oracle price scaling by 10**decimals / mulDiv overflows for high-decimal reference tokens → oracle unusable (revert) for legitimate tokens

no-min-position-size-dust-baddebt.description: no minimum loan/position size → dust positions are unprofitable to liquidate → underwater dust accumulates into protocol bad debt (sprayable)

wrong-router-method-integration-revert.description: an integration calls a DEX/router with the wrong method/selector/param-struct for the deployed target → the core path (swap/zap/migrate) always reverts; verify against the target's actual ABI, not an assumed interface

cross-chain-inbound-source-unauthenticat.description: an inbound cross-chain message handler fails to verify BOTH the local canonical endpoint caller AND the encoded trusted-remote (srcChain,srcAddr) → anyone forges/executes bridged messages (receiveFromBridge no caller gate; onlyOrigin can't bind msg.sender through a gateway callback)

approve-zero-reverts-blocks-teardown.description: approve(_,0)/safeApprove(_,0) in a market-removal/integration-teardown path reverts for tokens that disallow zero approval → removal permanently bricked (sibling of transfer-on-zero-revert)

stale-intermediate-state-gate.description: a close/reset/finalize decision reads state computed mid-operation, before the op's own later effect (health checked after repay but before slash) → gate fires on stale state, enabling window reset/grief

multiplier-default-zero-not-one.description: a multiplicative accumulator/index/multiplier left at storage-default 0 instead of ONE (1e27/1e18) → zeroes the whole product until a branch sets a floor (first borrowers pay 0 rate)

pause-blocks-derisk-path.description: a pause/guard meant for risk-adding actions also blocks the risk-reducing path (repay/liquidate/withdraw), often via a transitive helper (interest realization/index sync) → users can't cure positions → forced bad debt

stranded-reward-swept-by-next-caller.description: rewards pushed to a distributor that early-returns on a zero-state (zero coverage/stake) without refund/revert are stranded, then swept to a different recipient by the next distribute() that reads balanceOf(this)

liquidation-sizing-ignores-bonus.description: max-liquidatable/target-repay sized to reach target health omits the bonus/penalty collateral the liquidation also removes → post-liquidation health still below target → repeated/over-liquidation

zero-amount-external-call-reverts.description: an unconditional external deposit/distribute/swap/borrow with a computed amount that can be 0, to a protocol that rejects zero (Symbiotic DefaultStakerRewards InsufficientReward) → DoS of the calling flow

bps-sqrt-precision-loss.description: a bps/percentage param transformed through integer sqrt (100*sqrt(10000±bps)) and cached as a price bound loses precision → realized bound deviates from configured %

round-boundary-decay-reset.description: a linear decay/accrual n=elapsed*step/period that resets time-ref only when n<=0 is gameable by interacting when n rounds to 1 (elapsed<<period) → banks a full step for a fraction of the period, halving the decay period

controller-fed-pre-fee-amount.description: a fee/PID/rate controller updated post-trade is fed the pre-fee gross amount instead of the actual settled (post-fee minted/received) amount → controller drifts (fee grows wrong)

pct-cap-below-abs-floor.description: a relative cap MAX=pct*balance and an absolute floor require(input>MIN) co-gate the same input → dust balance makes MAX<MIN so no input is valid → soft DoS / vault brick

lz-ordered-execution-option-missing.description: a LayerZero OApp enforces ordered/sequential inbound delivery on the RECEIVE side (require nonce==inbound_nonce+1) but the SEND side builds options WITHOUT addExecutorOrderedExecutionOption() (only addExecutorLzReceiveOption gas/value). LZ then does not guarantee ordered delivery -> out-of-order messages hit the strict nonce check and revert, while the source chain already committed the state change -> cross-chain balance/state desync, stuck funds. Check BOTH sides agree: ordered-execution option on send <-> nonce enforcement on receive. e.g. Orderly SolConnector.withdraw omits the ordered-execution option while the Solana vault enforces inbound_nonce+1 under order_delivery.

solana-account-count-config-mismatch-pan.description: the number of accounts a handler slices/iterates is derived from a DIFFERENT quantity than the one actually provided/needed (e.g. a threshold vs a length, or a stored count vs the passed remaining_accounts), so indexing runs out of bounds and PANICS -> liveness/DoS (and on Solana the whole tx fails). Distinct from generic remaining_accounts-trust: here the COUNT arithmetic is wrong, not the per-account validation. LZ uln M-3.3.

solana-ed25519-introspection-data-unboun.description: a Solana program verifies a signature by INTROSPECTING a sibling ed25519_program (or secp256k1) instruction (sysvar instructions), but the pubkey/message the program ultimately TRUSTS is read from a SEPARATE source (an instruction ARG / a different account) that is bound to the verified bytes ONLY by offset arithmetic — with no check that the trusted bytes ARE the bytes the precompile verified. An attacker adjusts the attacker-controlled offset (e.g. message_offset) + calldata layout so the ed25519 program verifies a VALID signature for THEIR key over THEIR bytes, while the program reads a TRUSTED signer's pubkey + arbitrary payload from the separate source -> SIGNATURE BYPASS / oracle forgery. Pyth Lazer 3.1 (Critical). RULE: read the pubkey+message the program trusts FROM the precompile-verified instruction data itself, or assert the trusted buffer is byte-identical to (and at the claimed offset within) the verified instruction data.

solana-anchor-idl-instructions-enabled.description: Anchor by default injects on-chain IDL instructions into every program; the IDL is stored at a PDA managed by those instructions. If the IDL account is left UNINITIALIZED, ANY entity can call the IDL instruction to create it and become its AUTHORITY, then store arbitrary buffers — and program-owned PDAs are often treated as trusted/verified by clients, so a malicious IDL can mislead integrators. RULE: disable the IDL instructions in production (no-idl / no-default-idl build, or `anchor idl close`/init it under program control), or initialize+lock the IDL PDA authority at deploy. Drift (Zellic). Generalizes to ANY Anchor program.

vote-power-stranded-on-gauge-removal.description: users allocate a consumable resource (voting power/weight/allowance) to a registry entry, but the de-allocation/withdraw path require()s the entry still be valid -> removing/disabling the entry strands the allocation forever (user also can't re-allocate elsewhere). Fix: allow the set-to-zero/withdraw branch on removed entries. neobase H-01 (vote_for_gauge_weights require gauge_type>=0).

slope-underflow-dos.description: a time-decay checkpoint loop does `slope -= changes[t]` assuming slope was built via the same increment path; an admin direct-setter that writes bias/weight WITHOUT the matching slope makes the decrement underflow -> permanent revert bricking every read-path consumer (claims/withdraws). neobase M-01 (change_gauge_weight sets bias not slope -> _get_weight underflow). Underflow-guard decrements + admin setters must maintain the same invariants.

governance-weight-override.description: an admin setter writes a value that is normally DERIVED/accumulated by user actions (votes->gauge weight, deposits->total), bypassing the conservation invariant and letting the aggregate exceed what backs it -> reward/allocation skew. neobase M-03 (change_gauge_weight). Prefer adjusting inputs or removing the setter.

masterchef-rewarddebt-rounding.description: MasterChef rewardDebt adjustment on deposit/transfer rounds DOWN (floor) instead of in the protocol's favor -> repeated tiny position changes undercount debt and bank dust rewards (free claim); cumulative shortfall can revert the last claimer. neobase M-05 (sync_ledger rewardDebt += delta*accPerShare/1e18 floor). Round the debt-add UP.

unlock-override-free-vote.description: a global early-exit/override flag relaxes the EXIT (withdraw/unlock) constraint but the ENTRY functions (createLock/deposit/increase) are not also guarded -> user enters, consumes the time-weighted benefit (vote/boost), and exits in one tx for free (flash-loaned benefit). neobase M-07 (unlockOverride checked in withdraw not createLock/increaseAmount -> free gauge vote). Guard entry+benefit with the same flag or snapshot net of same-block exit.

memory-copy-state-write-lost.description: a storage struct is loaded into MEMORY then a field (status/flag) is written on the copy -> not persisted; the security-relevant effect (cancel/disable/mark-used) silently no-ops and the entity stays active. init-capital M-02 (fillOrder cancels `Order memory` copy not storage). Write to storage.

unconditional-native-refund-dos.description: a refund/sweep modifier unconditionally unwraps WNATIVE and pushes native to msg.sender with require(success) on EVERY call -> reverts for contract callers without payable receive, even on non-native ops. init-capital M-01 (refundNative). Make native refunds conditional/pull-based, don't hard-revert.

strict-equality-balance-dos.description: strict `==` equality on a post-external-call/post-swap balance reverts on any over-delivery/dust/rounding -> DoS. init-capital M-03 (coreCallback CloseExactOut require(balanceOf==amtOut)). Use >= and handle surplus.

deadline-blocktimestamp-noop.description: DEX/router call passed deadline=block.timestamp -> deadline always satisfied -> no mempool/delay protection. Thread a user deadline. particle M-02.

missing-liquidity-slippage.description: Uni mint/increase/decrease/collect or swap with amount*Min:0 / amountOutMinimum:0 -> no slippage/sandwich protection. Thread user mins. particle M-15.

global-param-change-affects-open-positio.description: admin setter changes a global term (loan duration/threshold/fee) read by ALREADY-OPEN positions' eligibility math -> instant default/reprice. Snapshot per-position at open or timelock. particle M-05 (updateLoanTerm).

reward-folded-into-liquidation-condition.description: liquidation reward deducted from premium/collateral BEFORE the eligibility comparison -> positions liquidatable earlier than true collateralization warrants. Evaluate eligibility pre-reward. particle M-06.

stale-snapshot-before-mutation.description: a value snapshotted+persisted BEFORE a same-function mutating call that changes it -> stale baseline used later (e.g. feeGrowthInside read before decrease/collect). Snapshot after mutations. particle H-02.

ported-uni-0.8-underflow-revert.description: Uni-V3 fee-growth/tick math relies on intentional 0.7 wraparound; ported to >=0.8 WITHOUT `unchecked` the subtractions revert -> DoS of fee/close/liquidate ops. Wrap ported uni math in unchecked. particle H-04.

blacklist-token-push-refund-dos.description: mandatory PUSH of a blacklistable token (USDC/USDT) to a fixed/counterparty recipient on a withdraw/close/refund path -> permanent DoS if recipient blacklisted (blocks both legs / the LP's liquidity). Pull-over-push + per-token recipient. particle H-01/M-08.

act-on-unowned-external-asset.description: entrypoint operates on an external NFT/position by id without verifying the contract owns/registered it -> state/credit created against an unheld/foreign asset. Gate on ownership/registration. particle M-12.

oz-quorum-fraction-percent-misuse.description: OZ GovernorVotesQuorumFraction(N) = N% of supply (N/100), NOT 1/N; passing a small N intending a large fraction (comment says '25%' but arg 4 => 4%) lets adversaries pass proposals with tiny voting power. General: verify security-critical constants against the LIBRARY's actual unit, don't trust the inline comment/NatSpec. iq-ai H-01.

aa-wallet-cross-chain-address.description: cross-chain reward/refund/credit attributed to a source-chain userAddress/beneficiary and paid on the destination chain assumes the address is the same user everywhere -- true ONLY for EOAs. Account-abstraction / smart-contract wallets (Safe, ERC-4337, smart-wallet factories) have a DIFFERENT address per chain, so the destination payout is stranded or seizable. Require an explicit destination-recipient or EOA/counterfactual-equivalence check. nudgexyz M-03.

tx-initiator-not-verified.description: a trusted relayer/router/executor (SWAP_CALLER, paymaster, solver) forwards a caller-supplied beneficiary/userAddress that is NOT bound to the real action initiator -> attacker sets an arbitrary beneficiary (e.g. a Uniswap V2 pool) and harvests the full reward/credit. Privilege of the CALLER is conflated with authorization of the BENEFICIARY. Bind the beneficiary via signature / token-source proof / participant registry. nudgexyz M-04.

division-as-percentage-fee.description: a fee/share computed as `amount / feeParam` is `amount*(1/feeParam)`, NOT a percentage; it only matches intent at the one default value and breaks silently when the (often misleadingly-named: taxCut/feePercent) param is changed. Use amount*rate/DENOMINATOR. traitforge H-03 (NukeFund.receive devShare=msg.value/taxCut, EntityForging devFee=forgingFee/taxCut).

stale-owner-snapshot-reward-attribution.description: reward/airdrop/credit keyed on a captured-at-creation address (initialOwner/firstMinter) that a LATER holder's action (burn/nuke/withdraw) can decrement -> the later owner griefs the original beneficiary. Verify the actor IS the beneficiary, or move the credit on transfer. traitforge H-02 (burn/nuke -> airdrop.subUserAmount(initialOwners[id])).

counter-reset-ignores-preexisting-entrie.description: a per-period cap enforced by a counter reset to 0 at rollover, while entries can be pre-seeded into the NEXT bucket (parallel path) before the reset -> the reset wipes the pre-seeded count and the new period exceeds its cap. Reset to the pre-seeded count, not 0. traitforge H-04 (_incrementGeneration sets generationMintCounts[gen]=0, discarding forged-into-next-gen entities -> >10k per gen).

cap-enforced-one-path-not-sibling.description: a max/limit checked in one entry function but omitted in a sibling function that mutates the same bounded variable -> the bound is bypassable via the unguarded path. Enumerate EVERY writer of a capped variable and confirm each enforces the bound (sibling-parity). traitforge H-05 (forge() checks newGeneration<=maxGeneration but _incrementGeneration increments currentGeneration with no cap -> infinite generations).

read-before-init-zero-default.description: a store filled incrementally (batched/lazy init) and consumed by a separate function with no completeness guard returns the zero/default for not-yet-written slots. Gate consumers on an initialized flag / index-bound, or init fully in the constructor. traitforge M-01 (getNextEntropy reads entropySlots before writeEntropyBatch* completes -> 0-entropy mint).

missing-slippage-dynamic-price-op.description: a mint/buy/redeem/claim whose price or payout is computed from mutable on-chain state (bonding curve, supply-based price, fund-share redemption) with no caller-supplied slippage bound (maxPrice/minOut/minClaim) -> adverse-movement + sandwich/front-run exposure. traitforge M-04 (mintWithBudget no max price) + M-16 (nuke() no minClaim).

no-exit-path-fund-lockup.description: pooled value whose ONLY withdrawal is gated on a condition that can become permanently unreachable (last NFT/share burned, expired deadline) with no admin/emergency drain -> indefinite lockup. Enumerate all exits; ensure one is always reachable or add gated emergency withdraw. traitforge M-02 (NukeFund fund exits only via nuke() requiring a live mature NFT).

signature-missing-chainid-replay.description: an off-chain signature consumed on-chain that does NOT commit to block.chainid (nor an EIP-712 domain that includes chainId) is replayable across every chain the protocol is deployed to. Confirm chainId is actually inside the signed struct; also require a nonce (same-chain replay) + deadline. phi H-01 (signatureClaim).

signature-scope-gap-unsigned-params.description: a signature/merkle proof is verified over SOME fields but the function acts on ADDITIONAL caller-supplied params not covered by the signed/proven set -> those params are attacker-malleable (impersonation/param-swap/frontrun). Diff signed fields vs acted-on fields; any acted-on field outside the signature is the bug. phi H-02 (createArt artist/receiver not bound) + M-05 (ref/artId/imageURI unvalidated).

map-entry-zeroed-not-removed-gas-dos.description: on full close, code does map.set(key,0) (or leaves a 0 entry) instead of map.remove(key), so the key stays in the enumerable structure forever; any function iterating the collection grows unbounded and eventually reverts on gas -> DoS. .remove() on exit; bound every loop over an enumerable structure. phi H-03 (Cred sets shareBalance to 0 -> CuratorRewardsDistributor.distribute bloats).

wrong-pausable-base-no-transfer-block.description: a token contract inherits generic PausableUpgradeable (only the whenNotPaused modifier) but NOT the token-specific pausable (ERC1155/ERC20/ERC721 Pausable) and never guards _update/_beforeTokenTransfer -> pause() does not actually block transfers (no-op emergency control). Confirm the transfer hook is whenNotPaused. phi M-01 (PhiNFT1155).

reentrancy-refund-before-state-finalize.description: a create/buy path refunds excess ETH (or makes any external call) BEFORE incrementing the id counter / writing the final record, so an attacker re-enters mid-write to overwrite or double-use the slot -- reentrant even though token/share balances were updated first. CEI must cover counters/records, not just balances; asymmetric guards (batch has nonReentrant, create doesn't) are a red flag. phi H-06 (createCred first-buy refund before credIdCounter++).

post-commitment-config-mutation.description: a creator/admin setter mutates terms users relied on when committing (soulbound, royalties, URI, mint window, fee, supply) with no immutability-after-start/timelock -> retroactive rug; also a require(endTime>=now) forces reopening a CLOSED window when editing. Terms holders depend on must be locked once the first participant commits. phi H-07 (post-mint settings) + H-04 (forced endTime reopen).

param-sanity-cap-wrong-unit.description: a require(param <= CONST) sanity guard in a setter where CONST is in the WRONG unit/scale vs the param's actual downstream use (a bps-looking 10_000/1e4 cap guarding an absolute wei amount, or vice-versa) -> the guard is meaningless or blocks legitimate config updates. Confirm MAX/MIN matches the param's real unit. CAP-site cousin of division-as-percentage-fee. phi M-02 (fee cap 10_000 vs wei fee).

cached-config-not-refetched.description: a mutable config value (fee destination, rate, dependency address) is copied from a source/registry into local storage at init; later source updates are not reflected -> stale config keeps routing funds to the old target. Read through to the source at use-time or add a refresh path. phi M-06 (PhiNFT1155 caches protocolFeeDestination from factory).

move-clmm-liquidity-overflow.description: wrong overflow/shift check or under-width intermediate in a CLMM wide-math/liquidity helper (checked_shlw/full_math/get_liquidity_from_amount/get_delta_*) lets an attacker mint oversized liquidity or pay ~dust for a large position (the Cetus $220M class)

move-rounding-direction.description: swap/liquidity/fee-growth division rounds the wrong way (toward the user) so a swapper or LP extracts value per call; pool-receives and user-receives legs must round in opposite, pool-favoring directions

move-signed-int-tick-math.description: i32/i64/i128 signed-int emulation or fee-growth-inside wrapping is mis-handled (abs/neg of MIN, wrong width, checked-subtract where Uniswap-v3 wrap is required, unbounded tick) -> wrong tick/fee accounting or position DoS

move-coin-balance-conservation.description: Coin/Balance split/join/zero handling breaks conservation: value created, dropped/locked, fee taken from wrong leg, or change/output sent to the wrong recipient

move-hot-potato-bypass.description: flash-loan/deferred-settlement hot-potato receipt is droppable (has drop/store) or repayment isn't enforced / is computed from manipulable state -> free flash loan or under-repayment

move-capability-safety.description: privileged entry lacks a genuine capability/witness/admin gate, or checks a Cap by type only without binding it to the specific object; or a witness/cap is forgeable; or version/upgrade gate missing -> unauthorized privileged action

move-object-ownership.description: function mutates/credits a per-user object (Position NFT, balance) without binding it to the caller -> attacker passes a shared or another user's object; shared-vs-owned confusion

move-constant-product-invariant-recheck.description: a swap/liquidity state-mutating math path never RE-ASSERTS the core conservation invariant (constant-product K = reserve_x*reserve_y non-decreasing, or the analogous curve invariant) on the post-mutation state; the absence of the guard is the finding even when current pricing is conservative -> a future pricing/fee/rounding change silently drains a reserve

move-public-helper-visibility.description: a SIDE-EFFECTING helper (event emitter, log/notify, state-touching util) is declared public fun instead of public(friend)/entry-guarded, so any external module/PTB can call it; for event emitters this forges protocol events without the underlying action, poisoning off-chain indexers/accounting/airdrop bots (distinct from move-capability-safety which is about privileged mutators)

fee-charged-outside-allowance.description: Fee-on-transfer charged from the owner outside the approved allowance in transferFrom: the allowance covers only the base amount but a fee hook debits extra from the owner, so a spender forces the owner to pay amount+fee beyond the approval.
fee-charged-outside-allowance.prompt_section: Fee charged OUTSIDE the approved allowance (fee-on-transfer in transferFrom)

forwarder-request-missing-deadline.description: A meta-tx / GSN ForwardRequest is nonce-protected but has no deadline/expiry, so a signed relayed request can be executed by a relayer at any later time against stale intent.
forwarder-request-missing-deadline.prompt_section: Meta-tx FORWARDER request has no deadline/expiry

unchecked-erc20-approve-return.description: Raw ERC20 approve()/transfer()/transferFrom() called without SafeERC20 and with the boolean return discarded; breaks on false-returning or no-return (USDT-style) tokens -> silent failure, stranded/escrowed funds.
unchecked-erc20-approve-return.prompt_section: Unchecked ERC20 approve()/transfer() return — raw call instead of SafeERC20

solana-lamport-invariant-includes-rent.description: A SOL accounting invariant compares an internal reserve field to a PDA's raw lamports() without subtracting the rent-exempt minimum, so the invariant is wrong by the rent amount (passes while short / mis-measures liquidity).
solana-lamport-invariant-includes-rent.prompt_section: SOL/lamport-balance invariant must EXCLUDE the rent-exempt minimum

fee-tier-boundary-discontinuity.description: A piecewise fee/rate curve is discontinuous at a tier boundary (the decay phase's boundary value does not meet the next flat phase), creating a timing-arbitrage cliff from a wrong slope/intercept.
fee-tier-boundary-discontinuity.prompt_section: Piecewise fee/rate curve DISCONTINUITY at a tier boundary
